_doc: Fork-and-flush autoresearch on surf_princessburglar_b26 (arXiv 2610.07447), the harness's second program (the first: surf_src_sidistic, ~/ar, 2026-10-20..23). Read autoresearch/README.md. Every number here is a HARD limit that box.py, the orchestrator and the fleet watchdog enforce; change it here, nowhere else.
goal: Pass surf_princessburglar_b26 from the TRUE map start (greedy eval; the start_run teleport destination, declared as the spawn in maps/surf_princessburglar_b26.zones.json): finish it, then finish it reliably, then faster than 75.18 s, the human world record (its demo on our zones, analysis only). Champion-free and generic (CLAUDE.md sections 0 and 0b): the record's time is the bar a result is read against, never a constant in the reward, the spawn rule or a schedule.
_field_doc: The grader's field is the goal graph WITHOUT corner cutting (build_goal_field no_corner_cut=True), the field the recipe shapes on (--race-no-corner-cut 1), at the recipe's lidar cell 32: 507,547 reachable voxels, start d 57,149 u (54,367 u on the corner-cutting field). Baked 2026-10-23 by the operator's local smoke run.
_score_episodes_doc: score.py counts only the first N episodes of an eval (header episode index < N): its score is a max over episodes, so an eval with more episodes would buy lottery tickets (r6b1 scored 98.418 with 54-episode evals of the incumbent's weights). 0 = all.
_rounds_doc: The user (2026-10-23): 'let's see if the sidistic recipe will converge quick on princess' - two rounds first, extended (with budget_end_hours) if it is progressing and the credit allows.
_max_boxes_doc: 4 branch boxes (box.py allows one per agent) + 1 spare. The droplet's ONE fleet watchdog daemon enforces its own cap from the first program's config; this program registers its boxes in that daemon's registry (RLSURF_FLEET_DIR=~/ar/fleet), or the daemon destroys them as unregistered.
_budget_end_hours_doc: Hours from THIS program's start (state.json started) over which box.py spreads the credit above the reserve: 2 rounds x 12 h + scoring. Move it with rounds.
offer_query: num_gpus=1 cuda_vers>=12.8 reliability>0.98 inet_down>300 rentable=true disk_space>60 cpu_cores_effective>=32 cpu_ghz>=2.5 verified=true
_cpu_exclude_doc: Regexes on the offer's cpu_name. vast's cpu_ghz is the TURBO clock (a Haswell E5-2696 v3 lists 3.8 GHz), so it does not catch old server parts: box 56818837, a 3090 on dual Xeon E5-2699 v3 (72 threads, Haswell 2014), trained the incumbent recipe at 57-59k steps/s with the trainer at 5,400% CPU and the GPU 5% busy, against 166-269k on 32-thread Zen 3 / Zen 4 / Raptor Lake hosts (2026-10-20).
_harness_files_doc: The operator's files: at the start of every round orchestrator.py restores them from the main checkout's HEAD over the winner's head, so a branch cannot carry its own caps, grader or rules forward, and the operator's fixes reach every round. autoresearch/NOTES.md is NOT one of them: it is the lineage's memory and travels with the winner. tools/bad_hosts.json is merged instead (the union of every branch's list).
_lineage_keys_doc: Keys of this file that belong to the lineage, not the operator: when the winner changed one during its round, its value travels into the next round's config.json (r1b1 made its scratch recipe the incumbent_recipe on 2026-10-20). Everything else here is restored from the operator's HEAD.
_offer_query_doc: Scratch training here is CPU-bound: the trainer takes half the container's CPUs for physics. A 16-thread 3090 box ran the incumbent recipe at ~36k steps/s (2026-10-20, smoke_x1) against ~420k on the 5090 PC, so boxes need >= 32 effective threads on a fast CPU. Measured the same night on a 3090 + Ryzen 9 5950X box (32 threads, quota 30.7 CPUs, omp 15): ~194k steps/s, GPU 30% busy.
_incumbent_recipe_doc: The sidistic lineage's final training flags (r7b2_bel, its first greedy finish), FROM SCRATCH: run_arm.sh SCRATCH's baseline is overridden by these (later flags win). Plus --maxvel 3500, the server's sv_maxvelocity in the WR demo's movevars (sidistic was trained at 4000).
_agent_prefix_doc: Agents pbr<round>b<k>, branches ar/pbr<round>b<k>: the first program's ar/r<n>b<k> are on origin.
